text.p: IXC Communications Inc said Monday that its previously announced plan to sell $100 million convertible preferred stock to two private investment groups has been terminated as the result of a disagreement between the company and one of the investment groups.

The other investment group indicated that it will instead purchase $25 million of a $100 million offering of a new series of convertible preferred stock to be offered to qualified institutional buyers under SEC Rule 144A, subject to final regulatory approval, a statement issued by IXC said.
The company said it expects the closing of that offering before the end of March 1997.

IXC said it believes that the $100 million 144A offering will meet its current capital needs, including providing adequate funds for completion of the 7,180 route mile expansion to the company's fiber network.

In addition to the private placement, the company had planned a secondary offering common stock, but said today it decided to withdraw the registration statement for the secondary offering, in part because of the recent market decline in the price of the company's common stock.
